activities.title: Yeast fermentation in sugar solution
activities.summary: Yeast in glucose solution produces CO₂ bubbles — demonstrates anaerobic respiration (fermentation).

activities.title: Starch test in leaf
activities.summary: Iodine test on boiled leaf — green parts turn blue-black showing starch formed by photosynthesis.

activities.title: Observation of stomata
activities.summary: Peel lower epidermis of leaf, stain with safranin, observe stomata and guard cells under microscope.

activities.title: Water rise through xylem
activities.summary: Plant stem in coloured water — dye rises through xylem vessels visible in cross-section.

activities.title: Transpiration in plants
activities.summary: Plastic bag tied around leaf shows water droplets inside — proof of transpiration.

activities.title: Heartbeat with stethoscope
activities.summary: Listen to lub-dub sounds of heart valves closing during cardiac cycle.

activities.title: Pulse rate after exercise
activities.summary: Compare pulse rate at rest and after exercise — heart pumps faster to meet O₂ demand.

activities.title: Dialysis tubing model
activities.summary: Visking tubing in water models selective permeability like kidney dialysis membrane.

exercise_mcqs.question: The kidneys in human beings are a part of the system for
exercise_mcqs.explanation: Kidneys filter blood and remove nitrogenous wastes (urea) as urine — part of the excretory system.

exercise_mcqs.question: The xylem in plants are responsible for
exercise_mcqs.explanation: Xylem vessels transport water and dissolved minerals from roots upward to leaves and other parts.

exercise_mcqs.question: The autotrophic mode of nutrition requires
exercise_mcqs.explanation: Autotrophic nutrition (photosynthesis) needs CO₂, water, chlorophyll to trap light, and sunlight as energy source.

exercise_mcqs.question: The breakdown of pyruvate to give carbon dioxide, water and energy takes place in
exercise_mcqs.explanation: After glycolysis in cytoplasm, pyruvate enters mitochondria where it is completely oxidised aerobically to CO₂, H₂O, and ATP.

intext_samples.question: Why is diffusion insufficient to meet the oxygen requirements of multicellular organisms like humans?
options: Multicellular organisms do not need oxygen
Most cells are not in direct contact with the environment
Diffusion is too fast for large bodies
Oxygen cannot diffuse through cell membranes
intext_samples.explanation: In large organisms most cells are deep inside the body and too far from the surface for diffusion alone to supply O₂ quickly enough.

intext_samples.question: Where does photosynthesis primarily occur in a green plant?
options: Green parts of the plant, especially leaves
intext_samples.explanation: Chloroplasts in green parts (mainly mesophyll of leaves) carry out photosynthesis using chlorophyll.

intext_samples.question: Which enzyme begins starch digestion in the human mouth?
intext_samples.explanation: Salivary amylase (ptyalin) in saliva converts starch to maltose in the buccal cavity.

intext_samples.question: Breathing and respiration are not the same because
options: Breathing is biochemical breakdown of glucose
Respiration is only inhaling and exhaling air
Breathing is ventilation; respiration releases energy from food in cells
intext_samples.explanation: Breathing moves air in and out of lungs; cellular respiration is the enzyme-controlled release of energy from glucose inside cells.

intext_samples.question: Food synthesised in leaves is transported to other parts of the plant through
intext_samples.explanation: Phloem translocates sucrose and other food materials from source (leaves) to sink organs.

intext_samples.question: The functional unit of the kidney that filters blood is the
intext_samples.explanation: Each nephron consists of glomerulus, Bowman's capsule, tubules, and collecting duct — filters blood and forms urine.
